note: Reviewed record of every dependency whose install-time lifecycle script (preinstall / install / postinstall, an implicit node-gyp rebuild via binding.gyp, or the prepare of a git-hosted dependency) pnpm may execute. pnpm is default-deny: a package not granted in pnpm-workspace.yaml#allowBuilds never runs its build. This file records WHICH decisions were reviewed and WHY a build is (or is not) necessary; pnpm-workspace.yaml remains the execution allow-list and scripts/check-install-scripts.mjs fails when the two disagree. Status-only: no secret value is read, stored or printed here.

packages.justification: First-party code in this repository: `prepare` runs `panda codegen`, which regenerates styled-system/ from panda.config.ts. Every typecheck / build / Storybook build resolves generated Panda CSS types from that directory, so a fresh clone cannot typecheck without it. The risk is this repository's own, reviewed in PR diffs.
packages.remediation: If Panda moves the codegen into a postinstall of a vendored package, move the record to that package and drop this entry.

packages.name: @biomejs/biome
packages.justification: Biome is the repository's only format/lint engine (AGENTS.md section 2 forbids ESLint/Prettier). Its postinstall resolves the platform package (@biomejs/cli-<platform>-<arch>) and writes the `biome` shim into node_modules/.bin; without it `pnpm run format:check` / `lint:check` have no binary and the whole validate:fast gate is dead.
packages.remediation: Biome ships platform binaries as optionalDependencies; if a future release links them without a postinstall, drop this entry and the pnpm allow-list line together.

packages.name: esbuild
packages.justification: Transitive build dependency of Vite / vite plugins. The postinstall validates that the platform binary package (@esbuild/<platform>) matches the JS shim and falls back to downloading it. Several versions are installed at once because Vite and its plugins pin different minors; each copy needs its own platform check, so a single allow-list name covers all of them.
packages.remediation: If a future esbuild resolves the binary purely through optionalDependencies, drop this entry and the allow-list line.

packages.name: workerd
packages.justification: The local Worker runtime binary used by @cloudflare/vite-plugin (SSR build) and by @cloudflare/vitest-plugin's workerd test pool. The postinstall links the downloaded platform binary into node_modules/.bin; without it `pnpm run test` (workerd pool) and the Cloudflare Vite plugin cannot start a runtime.
packages.remediation: workerd must keep shipping a postinstall until it publishes per-platform optionalDependencies; re-review on every version bump listed above.

packages.name: @infisical/cli
packages.justification: ELEVEST RISK ENTRY, reviewed deliberately. The preinstall (node src/index.cjs) fetches the platform `infisical` binary from the upstream GitHub release for the matching OS/arch into the package's own bin/ directory and marks it executable. It is necessary because the Infisical secret SoT tooling (ADR-0015: scripts/deploy-with-secrets.mjs, scripts/infisical-seed.mjs, scripts/check-cf-secrets.mjs and siblings) resolves @infisical/cli#bin and execs that native binary; with the script blocked those scripts fail closed. Recorded risk: install-time network fetch of an executable, with no checksum verification in the upstream script, and it runs at preinstall (before the rest of the install) rather than postinstall.
packages.remediation: Upstream change only (per Issue #474 scope: tool-side changes are a separate PR): ask Infisical to publish platform packages as optionalDependencies, or at minimum to move the fetch to postinstall and verify a published checksum. When that lands, drop this entry together with the pnpm allow-list line and record the removal in docs/runbook/install-script-audit.md.
